quote.text: From my governor, to be neither of the green nor of the blue party at the games in the Circus, nor a partisan either of the Parmularius or the Scutarius at the gladiators' fights; from him too I learned endurance of labor, and to want little, and to work with my own hands, and not to meddle with other people's affairs, and not to be ready to listen to slander.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Instill in your children the value of self-reliance by teaching them to work with their own hands and to focus on what truly matters, avoiding unnecessary distractions.
    • Encourage a life of simplicity and modest desires, so that they learn endurance and the virtue of not meddling in matters that do not concern them.
  • Leadership
    • Embrace impartiality by rising above partisan biases, ensuring your decisions are guided by the common good rather than by personal alliances or rivalries.
    • Lead through example by practicing diligence, humility, and a reluctance to indulge in gossip or slander, thus fostering respect and unity within your team.
  • Product Management
    • Adopt a disciplined focus on the essentials of your project, ensuring that each team member works diligently on their responsibilities without being derailed by external noise or politics.
    • Balance ambition with practicality by valuing steady progress and meaningful contributions over flashy results, thereby nurturing a culture of integrity and collaborative success.
